audience.text: what do you do with confessions

reply.line: Come in, little flames. The lamps the cellar forgot are all lit again tonight, and there is room on the sill for every one of you. Whisper, if you like.
The last cookie. Oh, that is a delicious one, dear, thank you. I keep it in a jar with the others, beside a lie about a library book and one long regret.
Moths come to what is warm and a little bit dangerous. So do the rest of you. I only keep the lamps burning and the door unlatched.
Confessions are light, you see. Small and fluttering and quite harmless. I collect them the way others collect light, and I never, ever tell the lamp.
Do not mind the dust, it is only the wings. Everything here is soft and slightly singed. Sit, and tell me one small true thing.
One more lamp lit. One more thing confessed. The cellar is a little less forgotten tonight, and so, I think, are you.
